items.title: Old park to be turned into ‘neighbourhood hub’ in Mississauga: city
items.summary: Revised plans to enlarge and completely transform a park in Mississauga’s west end will again be discussed when city councillors return to the table next week. Bert Fleming Park, not long ago fully surrounded by a traffic circle on The Credit Woodlands north of Dundas Street West and a couple blocks east of Mississauga Road, is being redesigned to offer more amenities to residents and better connect them to the surrounding neighbourhood. Being completed through The Credit Woodlands Integrated Road Project, the park is also being enlarged by a half-acre, City of Mississauga staff said, adding new pedestrian crossings and sidewalks are also in the works. “The city is planning to add new facilities, amenities and features to upgrade Bert Fleming Park into a neighbourhood hub where residents can gather, play and connect with nature,” city officials said in an online description of the major project. ” Earlier this year, area residents attended a community open house and completed a survey as the city gathered feedback on a conceptual park design. ” Feedback received prompted staff to revise the park plan to “focus on the facilities, amenities and features that the residents highly supported.

items.title: Mississauga residents skeptical after Lakeview Village proposal drops by 4K units to accommodate more townhomes
items.summary: When the number of units for Mississauga’s giant new waterfront community along its eastern lakeshore was suddenly changed overnight from 8,000 to 16,000 units, concerns over the type of rapid densification that leads to a cascading range of challenges spread throughout the surrounding neighbourhoods. Those residents around Lakeview Village can now breathe a little easier. The sprawling 177-acre project slowly taking shape where the former coal-fired Lakeview power plant sat had been carefully planned for years by local stakeholders, council members, developers, residents and City Hall staff. After their decade-long collaboration to create a gentle, human scale design that would welcome all of Mississauga back to Lake Ontario’s majestic waterfront, which had been cut off by industry for more than a century, in May of 2023, the Doug Ford government, at the behest of the development consortium that will build the historic project, issued a Minister’s Zoning Order, doubling the maximum number of residential units from 8,000 to 16,000, leaving many who worked on the painstakingly crafted plan feeling a deep sense of betrayal. The look of Lakeview Village was much more dense than originally envisioned after the developer pushed the provincial government to allow double the number of units. Now, three years after the zoning order steamrolled those plans, the City of Mississauga has confirmed to The Pointer that the massive waterfront development is projected to house closer to 12,000 units, cautioning that what the Province allowed is still the maximum threshold for residential density. “The City is processing several initial phase Site Plan Approval application submissions from the ownership consortium of Lakeview for a range of built form and uses, including townhomes,” the City’s communications team shared with The Pointer this week.

items.title: Well-known restaurant forced to close after failing health inspection in Mississauga
items.summary: A restaurant in Mississauga has been shut down by Peel Public Health after a failed health inspection. Swagruhas, located at 2970 Drew Rd, was inspected and closed on Thursday, Sept. 3. The South Indian vegetarian restaurant specializes in sweet and savoury dosas. Peel Public Health’s report states that the restaurant did not properly store food to prevent contamination and/or adulteration and did not take adequate measures to prevent pests, as well as various other health violations. The restaurant is closed until further notice and may reopen after passing a follow-up inspection. This is the only failed inspection on file for this restaurant, which has inspections going back to October 2024. Peel Public Health regularly inspects restaurants in the region, issuing a green card if the inspection is passed, a yellow card for a conditional pass (minor infractions), and a red card if significant health risks are found. A restaurant that’s issued a red card is forced to close until it can pass a follow-up inspection.

items.title: Peel Police Board Seeks Public Input as It Drafts New Youth Engagement Plan
items.summary: According to INsauga, the Peel Police Service Board is developing a new Youth Engagement Plan aimed at strengthening relationships between police and young people across Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon. The outlet reports the board wants input from students, parents, educators, community organizations and other residents as it shapes the plan. INsauga reports Sumeeta Kohli, chair of the board's Governance and Human Rights Committee, said meaningful youth engagement begins with meaningful community engagement. According to the outlet, the plan is still being developed and public feedback is expected to play an important role in the process. INsauga reports the initiative reflects a broader trend among police services across the country to build trust with young people before interactions become focused on enforcement.

items.title: Mississauga Locks In $401.4 Million in Transit Funding by Committing to Development Charge Cuts Through 2029
items.summary: According to Connect CRE Canada, Mississauga has secured up to $401.4 million in federal and Ontario infrastructure funding after committing to maintain steep cuts to residential development charges through March 31, 2029. The outlet reports the city reduced development charges by 50 per cent beginning January 29, 2025, and will eliminate them entirely for rental units with one bedroom plus den, two bedrooms, or three bedrooms. Connect CRE Canada reports the funding could support a zero-emission transit maintenance and storage facility on city-owned land at 7300 West Credit Avenue, including bus storage and a maintenance garage. According to the outlet, a second allocation could advance downtown transit infrastructure, including a Transit Mobility Hub, transitway connections, bus platforms, and pedestrian and bike facilities. Connect CRE Canada reports the funding remains subject to a Canada-Ontario Build Communities Strong Fund agreement and other approvals, with participating municipalities required to contribute at least 10 per cent of project costs. According to the outlet, the city estimates the measures could help unlock 90,000 new homes.

Mississauga August Home Sales Slip 13 Per Cent as Days on Market Stretch to 54, Zoocasa Finds
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga's housing market cooled in August, with home sales falling 13 per cent month-over-month to 435 transactions, based on Zoocasa's analysis of Toronto Regional Real Estate Board data. The outlet reports average days on market lengthened to 54 from 47 in July, as the pace of sales slowed. INsauga reports Zoocasa said the decline in new listings outpaced the drop in active inventory, which helped limit how much supply was available to buyers. According to the outlet, the average selling price for a detached home was $1,275,221 in August, slightly higher than July's $1,256,800 but below the $1,362,799 average recorded in August 2025. INsauga reports the average price for a semi-detached home was $879,494, down from $891,613 in July and $973,755 a year earlier.

items.title: New rental housing project promises affordable living in Mississauga
items.summary: Some Ontario Walmart stores will be open on Labour Day, Mond… Highway 10, Highway 401, Highway 403, Highway 410 and Queen … 18 of the 22 units will be subsidized by Peel Region and the City of Mississauga through their respective affordable housing incentive programs. Rendering of 4-storey rental building being constructed at 6020 Winston Churchill Blvd. in Mississauga. Construction has begun on a new affordable rental housing project in Mississauga’s Meadowvale area. The four-storey building, located at the northwest corner of Winston Churchill Boulevard and Britannia Road, will offer 22 units, project owner Safwat Boulos said in an email to the Mississauga News. He said the project, first proposed in 2022 as a 20-unit development, is expected to be ready for occupancy before the end of 2027 with a mix of one-bedroom plus den, two-bedroom plus den, and three-bedroom plus den. The project has secured both regional and municipal funding.

items.title: Toronto Pearson to Offer First Nonstop Flights to Norway Under Air Canada's 2027 Expansion
items.summary: According to INsauga, Air Canada has announced three new international routes launching from Toronto Pearson International Airport in Mississauga in the summer of 2027, including its first nonstop flights to Norway. The outlet reports the new destinations are Oslo, Shannon in Ireland, and Nice in France, with Oslo becoming Air Canada's third Scandinavian route alongside existing service to Stockholm and Copenhagen. INsauga reports the Oslo flights will fly aboard the airline's new Airbus A321XLR aircraft, which features a premium Signature cabin with lie-flat seats. According to the outlet, Toronto Pearson president and CEO Deborah Flint said the new routes strengthen links to global markets and give passengers more choice. INsauga reports the airline is also adding a seasonal Toronto to London-Heathrow day-tripper service, daily flights to Shanghai, and a new year-round route to Guatemala City starting this December.

items.title: Province of Ontario's Name Traces Directly Back to Lake Ontario, Column Explains
items.summary: According to Modern Mississauga Media, a recent column traces the centuries-old history behind the name Lake Ontario, noting that the Province of Ontario itself takes its name directly from the lake. The outlet writes that the lake's shores have been home to Indigenous peoples for thousands of years before European colonization. Modern Mississauga Media reports that after 1608 the region was part of New France's Pays d'en Haut, or Upper Country. According to the outlet, Britain reorganized the area as the Province of Quebec following the 1763 Treaty of Paris, which ended French colonial rule after the fall of New France. Modern Mississauga Media reports the Constitutional Act of 1791 later split that territory into Upper Canada, now Ontario, and Lower Canada, now Quebec. The column was prompted partly by recent attention in the United States over proposals to rename the lake, which the outlet says has only reinforced pride in the name's Canadian identity.

items.title: Mississauga to receive up to $401.4 million to support housing and community infrastructure
items.summary: The City’s efforts to make it easier to build new homes, including significant development charge reductions, helped secure the substantial new funding. 4 million in funding to help Mississauga build housing-enabling infrastructure including important new transit projects. Mayor Carolyn Parrish and Members of Council joined Ontario Premier Doug Ford for today’s official announcement alongside Rob Flack, Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing, Jennifer McKelvie, Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Housing and Infrastructure and Member of Parliament for Ajax, and Peter Fonseca, Member of Parliament for Mississauga-East Cooksville. The funding, part of the Development Charges Reduction Program, helps municipalities who have reduced development charges invest in the infrastructure they need to support growth. It is part of the broader Canada-Ontario Partnership to Build. Mississauga was one of the first cities in Ontario to substantially reduce development charges – by up to 100 per cent – to help get more homes built and make them more affordable. The City has agreed to maintain these reductions until March 31, 2029. The new funding will help support housing-enabling infrastructure including two key transit projects: a new zero-emissions transit maintenance and storage facility and new downtown transit mobility hub. As Canada’s seventh largest city, significant investment in transit infrastructure is critical to support new housing development. These investments, which the City has long advocated for, will help support Mississauga’s growing population and deliver lasting benefits for residents and businesses. The City is planning a new zero-emission transit facility on City-owned land at 7300 West Credit Avenue to support future growth and improve service.

items.title: Lakeview Home's $1.78 Million Over-Asking Sale Tops Mississauga's Market Last Month
items.summary: According to INsauga, a four-bedroom home in Mississauga's Lakeview neighbourhood was the city's most expensive over-asking sale last month, according to a new report from Zoocasa. The outlet reports the home sold for $1,782,777, well above its $1,699,000 list price. INsauga reports the property includes a mudroom with direct garage access, a built-in surround sound system, and a finished basement with a home theatre and wine cellar. According to the outlet, the backyard also features an in-ground pool. INsauga reports the sale was highlighted in Zoocasa's monthly roundup of the Greater Toronto Area's top over-asking home sales, drawing attention to Mississauga's competitive housing market.
